text:
Alice: FYI — seeing weird east-west latency oscillations between GPU nodes during the 12:30-13:00 batching window. p99 token latency jumped ~10x for several pods. Anyone else?
Ben: Can you share the grafana link and which region/cluster?
Alice: grafana: https://grafana.internal/redwood/ew-latency?orgId=1 (look at cluster-gpu-eu-2, pod group rtf-*)
Alice: p95 ~22ms -> p95 ~180ms, p99 went from 60ms -> 600ms. Packet retransmits up on the NIC counters.
Carla_M: Do we have jumbo frames enabled consistently? Last time I saw weird EW fragmentation it was an MTU mismatch.
Alice: Good call — some nodes were on 9000, others on 1500 after last week's image roll. I captured `ip link` on node-04 and node-11: 
```
node-04: mtu 9000 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
node-11: mtu 1500 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
```
Ben: That would explain bursts during large batched transfers. But retransmits also point to queueing/egress drops — what do `ethtool -S` counters show?
David: Also check if RDMA/ROCE traffic is enabled on those NICs. If PFC/DSCP isn't configured and some hosts try RoCE while others don't, you'll see microbursts and tail latency.
Erin: We don't intentionally use RoCE in eu-2, but some instance types get mlx5 with drivers that expose RDMA by default. I saw `mlx5_core` loaded on a subset after the kernel update.
infra-bot: alert: network.egress.drops cluster-gpu-eu-2 node-11 spikes detected (count: 420 -> 3200)
Carla_M: Can you post `tc qdisc show dev eth0` and `dmesg | grep -i net` from impacted nodes?
Alice: Posted snippets in the incident gist: https://gist.internal/abcd1234 — `tc` shows fq_codel on some hosts and pfifo_fast on others.
Ben: Mixed qdisc + MTU mismatch + RDMA driver noise = perfect storm during big kv cache transfers.
David: Short-term mitigation: force batching window reduction to lower concurrent east-west throughput for next 2 hours. Also we can apply `ethtool -K eth0 tso off gso off gro off` on the 1500-MTU hosts to reduce fragmentation impact.
Erin: I can roll a daemonset patch to unify qdisc -> `fq_codel` and set MTU to 9000 across the pool, but that requires a rolling reboot for kernel to reattach drivers cleanly for mlx5. Risky during peak.
Carla_M: Alternative: enable ECN/DCTCP on the hypervisor/host side and tune `net.core.netdev_max_backlog` and `txqueuelen` to avoid packet drops during microbursts. Example commands: `sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_ecn=1` and `sysctl -w net.core.netdev_max_backlog=5000`.
Alice: I'm going to temporarily reduce max_batch_tokens from 4096 -> 2048 and set per-pod egress limit via `tc` to smooth peaks. Rolling out now.
Ben: Please post the rollout command snippet so SRE can watch.
Alice: Using: `kubectl patch deployment rtf-batcher -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"batcher","env":[{"name":"MAX_BATCH_TOKENS","value":"2048"}]}]}}}}'`
David: After that, check NIC tx drops and GPU throughput. If p99 stays high, we might need to isolate EW inference traffic to a separate VLAN or use SR-IOV for critical pools.
Erin: I'll prepare a node-daemonset to normalize MTU/qdisc but hold it until post-peak. Posting PR in a few mins.
Carla_M: Follow-up action: inventory all NICs for RDMA capability and kernel module state. I'll create a short script to report `ethtool -i`, `lsmod | grep mlx`, and MTU for every GPU node.
infra-bot: action_created: ticket #INF-4721 "ew-latency: MTU + qdisc drift analysis" assigned to Carla_M
Alice: Thanks. Early results: after reducing batch size, p99 dropped from 600ms -> ~120ms. We'll keep monitoring for the next hour. :thumbsup:
Ben: Great. Once post-peak, let's schedule a small maintenance window to standardize MTU/qdisc and decide RDMA posture across clusters.
David: Also add kernel NIC offload flag checks into our node health checks to catch regressions after image pushes.
Erin: PR: https://git.internal/r/infra/daemonsets/mtu-qdisc unify (WIP). I'll CC infra team.
Alice: Closing loop here — keeping thread open but moving to monitoring channel in 30m if stable.
